questions.prompt: Does every optional refusal require a detailed explanation?
questions.answer: No; a clear respectful refusal may be sufficient.

questions.prompt: How does a counterproposal differ from a refusal?
questions.answer: It declines the original terms while offering a feasible alternative.
questions.feedback: Do not offer an alternative you cannot deliver.

questions.prompt: What if declining affects an existing safety duty?
questions.answer: Use authorised handover, negotiation or escalation; do not abandon the duty.

questions.prompt: Should a learner always decline directly in an unsafe relationship?
questions.answer: No; safety and specialist support may be more appropriate than confrontation.
questions.feedback: Do not grade courage by direct refusal.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Selects and communicates a proportionate refusal or counterproposal while respecting duties, privacy, consent and safety.
scoring.transfer: Prepare three fictional refusal scripts and one counterproposal. Include an obligation check, an accessible communication option and a safe alternative route. Explain why an offer of alternative assistance must be realistic and voluntary.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
